items.title: Establish OBS adoption contracts, current baseline, and maintained acceptance fixture
items.problem: Operators cannot reliably distinguish shipped behavior from stale architecture descriptions, and the comparative fixture contains known parsing limitations that cannot serve unchanged as a CI verdict.
items.solution: Establish current, explicit product contracts and a maintained package-level acceptance runner that reports actual MCP results and OBS state.
stories: a baseline at the implementation commit and installed dependency lock
I can distinguish new regressions from the historical study
documentation that accurately describes available transports and controls
I can configure capabilities without relying on obsolete deferrals
documented settings and image compatibility contracts
existing integrations continue to work as fidelity improves
acceptance assertions that compare intended and observed OBS state
equivalent valid response forms to be interpreted correctly
a parser limitation does not become an invented server defect
unsupported fixture behavior to remain distinct from product failures
test infrastructure does not distort acceptance
every research finding linked to a work item or reasoned disposition
existing resource subscriptions and retention semantics verified
decisions: Retain TypeScript/Effect, schema-first request descriptors and operations, explicit toolsets, capability filtering, and existing stdio/stateful/stateless HTTP boundaries.

Record settings compatibility, opt-in full-fidelity access and sensitive-value policy, and native-image result compatibility before implementation lanes begin. Choose exact public names within existing conventions and record the choice in this issue.

Use current source and lockfile for new acceptance; keep the pinned September research evidence immutable. Maintain production acceptance infrastructure separately from historical benchmark snapshots.
Use a freshly installed package through MCP with a controlled OBS endpoint as the primary seam. Reuse existing protocol and HTTP tests for properties impractical at that seam.
Correct semantic extraction, PNG validity, timeout observation margins, and false-success adjudication before turning research probes into CI assertions.
Reconcile existing issue #2 against implemented stateful subscriptions and documented screenshot retention. Close or narrow it only with acceptance evidence, not from a title match.
Track known fidelity gaps as explicit pending contracts; completing this foundation does not falsely mark those implementation gaps fixed.

Add field-aware protocol/schema comparison that inspects actual descriptor/tool fields, reports deliberate restrictions separately, and detects newly omitted required or supported locator fields. Correct 147 request-name versus 146 exported-descriptor wording and preserve batch-only Sleep.

Preserve static registration and existing quality/registry checks. Do not adopt a fail-safe loader that silently skips malformed local modules; these are required product modules, not optional third-party plugins.
tests: Exercise real packaged entry initialization/listing, baseline scene/audio/record/image behavior, truthful errors, capability reduction, timeout and disconnect with deterministic fixture state.
Distinguish accepted mutation state, unknown outcome, valid alternative output shape, unavailable capability, and fixture-unimplemented requests.
Review documentation against actual tool/resource/transport contracts and confirm stateful/stateless subscription differences through existing HTTP tests.
Prove the runner detects representative known false-success and invalid-image cases without depending on implementation module layout.
Demonstrate that the field-aware audit detects representative missing/stripped fields and distinguishes explicit product restrictions from unsupported protocol requests.
items.out: Implementing all fidelity features, changing the framework/language, native OBS integration, publishing a package, and rerunning the entire competitor census.

items.title: Preserve scene UUID and canvas identity across public tools and batches
items.problem: Users cannot select some intended scenes or canvases because three official selector fields are absent from the public interface.
items.solution: Support the missing selectors consistently from listed schema through request dispatch and observable result.
stories: scene listing scoped by canvas UUID
input creation on a canvas selected with a scene name
the input is created in the intended place
renamed or ambiguous names do not select the wrong entity
batch and ordinary scene selection to follow the same locator contract
listed schemas to describe valid selector combinations
invalid or unsupported selectors to fail explicitly
the server does not silently fall back to another scene
valid name-based requests to remain compatible
upgrading does not break established workflows
decisions: Add canvasUuid to list_scenes and name-based create_input, and sceneUuid to set_current_scene.
Propagate supported locators through domain schemas, descriptors, operations, tools, relevant resources, and batch setters.
Follow the pinned official request's locator rules; do not invent uniform name/UUID precedence where request semantics differ.
Retain capability filtering and existing name-based contracts. Report unsupported behavior truthfully without dropping supplied identity.
tests: Through packaged MCP, assert exact outgoing fields and independently verify the selected/created entity in a multi-canvas, duplicate-name fixture.
Cover UUID-only, supported name/canvas combinations, name compatibility, invalid combinations, and corresponding batch behavior.
Use focused batch/protocol tests when necessary; do not pretend the historical fixture already implements complete batch semantics.
items.out: New canvas-management families, native process identity, broad scene editing, or a generic raw request escape hatch.

items.title: Provide explicit full-fidelity filter, output, and transition settings contracts
items.problem: Users cannot inspect and update nested or kind-specific OBS settings because current interfaces summarize or narrow values, and transition reads omit settings.
items.solution: Expose an explicit, bounded settings representation that preserves supported nested values and makes restrictions visible while keeping existing typed conveniences compatible.
stories: I can understand an existing filter before changing it
nested filter settings that retain supported unknown keys
encoder or output configuration is not silently lost
current transition settings on the valid existing read
I can inspect the transition OBS actually uses
my existing configuration automation keeps working
explicit sensitive-setting exclusions and opt-in boundaries
I understand what data a call can reveal
an update does not accidentally erase unrelated settings
I am not told a change succeeded when it was discarded
decisions: Use the foundation's recorded settings contract; keep lossless access explicit and retain existing typed convenience behavior.
Represent supported settings as bounded recursive JSON, including arrays, objects, booleans, strings, finite numbers and null; document limits and exclusions.
Preserve unknown permitted values within the selected settings contract. Sensitive-value exclusions must be explicit rather than silently implying an exact round-trip.
Expose transitionSettings from the existing valid current-transition request. Do not add the nonexistent GetCurrentSceneTransitionSettings request.
Specify OBS overlay/merge/replacement semantics for each write and avoid read-modify-write assumptions that overwrite concurrent changes.
Keep validation, request capability filtering, toolset policy, and truthful MCP error handling.
tests: Execute packaged MCP read/update/readback cases with nested objects, arrays, unknown permitted keys and representative plugin/output settings; compare actual fixture state.
Verify typed convenience compatibility, explicit opt-in behavior, sensitive-field policy, size/depth limits, malformed inputs and OBS rejections.
Assert current-transition settings are returned using a valid public request name and that excluded/rejected values never appear as successful writes.
items.out: Arbitrary code execution, indiscriminate secret exposure, accepting all unbounded input, a universal raw OBS dispatcher, or an exhaustive catalog of plugin-specific controls.

items.title: Return native MCP images and define remote screenshot save semantics
items.problem: Complete screenshot bytes are currently embedded in JSON, and save validation assumes compatible MCP/OBS filesystems, limiting reliable visual verification.
items.solution: Let supported clients consume bounded native MCP image results while preserving the agreed metadata contract and making save-location semantics explicit.
stories: a screenshot directly consumable by my MCP client
I can verify what OBS is showing
complete image content and MIME metadata
I do not need custom JSON-base64 extraction
upgrading does not break resource consumers
clear destination-host semantics for saved images
a path check on one machine is not mistaken for a write on another
visual checks do not create unbounded memory or files
I can choose a supported alternative
consistent tool and latest-screenshot resource behavior
I can correlate visual evidence with its capture
a recorded real OBS/client acceptance result
mock image validity is not mistaken for rendering proof
decisions: Use native MCP image tool content as the selected first-milestone path, with existing metadata retained compatibly. Preserve the existing latest-screenshot metadata resource and retention ownership; do not create a second image-retention surface.
Preserve complete bounded content, MIME metadata, configured toolsets and capability gating. Keep existing latest-screenshot resource lifetime explicit.
Define local/shared/remote filesystem behavior and truthful unsupported cases. Do not treat a local path check as proof of a remote OBS save.
Keep currently supported formats explicit; investigate capability-based format expansion only against a demonstrated supported format.
Retain path boundaries and bounded retention; document any opt-in filesystem assumptions.
tests: Through packaged MCP verify full image decoding, dimensions/content where applicable, payload bounds, malformed image rejection, tool/resource consistency and unsupported capabilities.
Reuse existing HTTP/resource tests for lifetime and transport semantics instead of creating parallel retention test infrastructure.
Before release, run an isolated real OBS capture with an actual supported MCP client and record that the image is consumable. Test the claimed save topology separately.
items.out: Visual AI judgments, automatic image-diff policy, unbounded screenshot history, OS-wide capture, or cross-platform window-management promises.

items.title: Prepare and gate publication of the exact OBS package that passes acceptance
items.problem: Initialization and tool-count smoke checks do not establish usable OBS behavior, and the publication path does not explicitly bind publication to the tested tarball.
items.solution: Extend existing package verification to the full reference workflow and prepare publication of the exact verified artifact, with attributable registry evidence required when the maintainer authorizes release.
stories: a package that completes the advertised OBS workflow
truthful failures from the installed package
my agent does not act on fabricated success
the tested tarball to be the published tarball
verified published identity, version and integrity
I can attribute the installed artifact
dependency updates cannot silently break entry
defaults and opt-in capabilities tested separately
the all-toolsets test does not misrepresent defaults
clear publication failure and retry behavior
an interrupted attempt does not justify overwriting conflicting artifacts
visual acceptance evidence linked to a release candidate
real-client checks refer to the intended build
decisions: Extend the existing package smoke, Node compatibility matrix and release flow; do not introduce a parallel packaging architecture.
Install the packed tarball in a clean consumer and execute MCP inspection, mutation/readback, recording, native image, capability/error and lifecycle assertions against controlled OBS.
Publish the same verified tarball and compare registry integrity, identity and version afterward. Preserve exact candidate/source/dependency provenance.
Exercise documented defaults as well as the explicit all-toolsets acceptance configuration; disclose configured timeout values.
Use existing authenticated publication policy. Never overwrite conflicting versions or move release references to conceal failures.
Implementation may prepare and verify artifacts; actual npm publication requires the maintainer's release authorization. Creating this planning issue is not publication authorization.
tests: Run meaningful packed-process acceptance on supported Node versions; verify resulting OBS state and MCP error semantics rather than only tool counts.
Test wrong/missing artifact identity and digest mismatches, registry lookup failures and conflicting publication states with controlled boundaries.
Require a green existing quality gate and recorded isolated real OBS/client visual acceptance for the selected artifact; do not put real OBS into deterministic default CI.
items.out: Publishing during spec creation, a native five-platform release matrix, unrelated package-manager migration, or rewriting existing authentication policy.

items.title: Add read-only AV-health diagnosis with explicit evidence and unknowns
items.problem: Users must manually combine low-level status calls and can confuse unavailable measurements with healthy audio/video.
items.solution: Provide one bounded read-only diagnostic workflow that reports observations, evidence-backed warnings, unknowns and supported next actions.
stories: I can locate likely recording or streaming problems
measured facts separated from inferred warnings
I understand how confident the diagnosis is
unknown or unsupported checks marked clearly
missing measurements are not called healthy
I can inspect a live session without changing it
diagnosis does not hang or accumulate data indefinitely
actionable recommendations tied to supported tools
I can address the reported problem
stable structured results with timestamps or freshness evidence
I can present the diagnosis accurately
decisions: Compose existing status, statistics, audio/output and resource operations; do not duplicate their connection or error policy.
Define observation windows, freshness, threshold provenance, unsupported measurements and cancellation before exposing results.
Do not infer successful live streaming, audible signal or actual rendered correctness merely from an active flag.
Keep the first workflow read-only. Use task-level vocabulary rather than exposing protocol implementation details.
tests: Execute the packaged MCP diagnostic against controlled healthy, degraded, unavailable, stale and disconnected fixture states; assert zero mutation requests.
Verify each warning points to observed evidence and that unknown measurements cannot become healthy defaults.

Validate modeled AV warning semantics with controlled OBS observations. Any later physical audio/device claim needs explicitly scoped real-environment evidence; such a manual follow-up is not silently added to the approved visual release gate.
items.out: Automatic repair, audio-chain mutation, continuous monitoring service, AI visual judgment, or guarantees about codecs/devices not actually measured.

items.title: Add preview/apply audio setup with bounded failure and restoration semantics
items.problem: Operators lack a task-level preview/apply path for useful audio setup and cannot safely reason about partial changes across multiple operations.
items.solution: Deliver one focused audio-setup workflow with an inspectable preview, explicit apply, postcondition evidence and conflict-aware partial-failure handling.
stories: a preview of planned audio changes
I can understand the effect before applying it
a stale preview does not change another input
acceptance is not mistaken for completion
partial progress and uncertain outcomes reported
I know which state may need attention
recovery does not overwrite another operator's work
a multi-step job cannot run indefinitely
the workflow does not promise unavailable plugins
one complete useful workflow before a generic engine
its behavior can be tested and maintained
decisions: Build on existing operations and the lifecycle investigation's verified contract; choose one documented audio setup profile and supported prerequisites.
Define preview lifetime, target identity, explicit apply, step results, terminal success/failure/unknown states and bounded execution.
Preserve the existing non-retry policy for uncertain in-flight mutations; do not silently repeat a possibly applied action.
Record affected state and compensate only where safe. Conflicts, disconnects or uncertain restoration remain explicit outcomes.
Keep preview/apply extensible for later tasks without building an arbitrary workflow interpreter.
tests: At packaged MCP level prove preview sends no mutations, stale previews are rejected or safely revalidated, successful apply matches state, and each injected step failure reports actual progress.
Cover applied-but-reply-lost, cancellation, reconnect, missing prerequisites and intervening external changes before restoration.

Verify the chosen audio profile and partial-apply cases through the controlled OBS fixture. Any physical audio-quality or platform-specific claim requires a separately scoped manual validation, beyond this issue's automated acceptance.
items.out: General scripting, automatic changes during diagnosis, broad scene/recording workflow families, or blind snapshot restoration.

items.title: Extend bounded OBS history into useful event and audio-meter diagnostics
items.problem: Existing bounded events and confirmations do not yet provide a complete user-facing explanation of recent changes or aggregated audio-meter evidence.
items.solution: Extend the existing event infrastructure only where it supports a concrete recent-history or AV diagnostic query.
stories: a derived explanation or media-liveness summary over the existing bounded recent-event API
I can understand why my session changed
summarized meter evidence rather than thousands of samples
I can assess levels without a data flood
gaps, overflow and stale intervals identified
absence of events is not mistaken for absence of change
diagnostics do not silently increase data collection
events correlated with relevant targets and operations
the history is useful for diagnosis
existing event and confirmation semantics preserved
new diagnostics do not duplicate or destabilize the event layer
decisions: Reuse existing bounded event buffers, resources and named confirmations; do not replace them with a second client/event store.
Define opt-in meter subscription groups, aggregation windows, memory bounds, overflow/gap markers, freshness and supported event families.
Keep screenshots, credentials and sensitive settings out of ordinary event summaries according to existing policy.
Distinguish diagnostic history from a durable audit log or proof that every external action was observed.
tests: Drive real MCP queries with controlled events, meter samples, overflow, reconnect and cancellation; assert bounded memory-visible behavior and truthful gaps.
Use focused existing event tests for scheduling/overflow boundaries and package-level tests for user-visible results.

Verify aggregation against controlled OBS meter samples. Do not claim actual audible quality or clipping diagnosis beyond what the measured values establish; physical-signal validation is a separately scoped follow-up.
Verify the diagnostic delta over the existing recent-event API and preserve its public behavior and bounded store; do not test a duplicate history implementation.
items.out: An unbounded event firehose, permanent audit database, generic arbitrary-event automation, or recreating already implemented confirmations.

items.title: Add grounded MCP prompts, completions and behavioral annotations
items.problem: Users and clients cannot easily discover supported task workflows or valid current identifiers, and behavior hints are absent.
items.solution: Expose capability-grounded prompts, supported MCP completion domains and accurate behavior annotations over existing operations.
stories: I can start a recording or diagnosis workflow without knowing tool names
I avoid stale or misspelled names
accurate read-only and destructive behavior hints
guidance does not refer to unavailable actions
I understand why suggestions may not appear
fresh bounded suggestions with identity context
duplicate names do not mislead me
annotations treated as hints rather than authorization
security does not depend on client interpretation
decisions: Use implemented workflows/tools/resources as the sole authority for prompt content and capability availability.
Support completion only at MCP-defined references supported by the client and protocol; do not promise universal tool-argument autocomplete.
Define bounded, fresh scene/source/input/filter/profile/collection suggestions consistent with locator identity and enabled capabilities.
Derive accurate read-only, destructive and idempotence behavior annotations from each public operation's actual semantics; hints do not grant permissions or replace validation.
Start with a small documented prompt set for existing recording, visual verification and health jobs.
tests: Use actual MCP handlers/clients to inspect prompts, supported completion requests and annotations under multiple toolsets/capability profiles.
Verify suggestions after rename/removal, duplicate names, unavailable OBS, cancellation and bounded result limits.
Test prompts against registered capabilities and expected task outcomes, not exact prose snapshots.
items.out: Inventing functionality through prompt text, undocumented tool-call autocomplete, or using behavior hints as security controls.

items.title: Add versioned preset diff and apply contracts over verified operations
items.problem: Operators cannot save and compare a supported known-good setup with clear version, secret and restoration behavior.
items.solution: Provide bounded, versioned presets with preview/diff and explicit apply for a deliberately chosen supported setup scope.
stories: save a supported setup as a named preset
diff a preset against current state
a preset does not unexpectedly change OBS
I can maintain my saved setups
sharing or retaining them does not expose secrets
old presets do not silently change meaning
recovery does not overwrite intervening work
decisions: Choose and document one persistence boundary (server state, OBS persistent data or explicitly scoped files) before implementation; do not silently use all three.
Start with the verified workflow's supported setup scope; record scope before broad scene/source/recording families are added.
Version schemas from the first release, define migration/rejection policy, storage limits, identity handling and sensitive-value exclusions.
Reuse preview/apply and restoration contracts rather than implementing a second mutation engine.
tests: Test save/read/diff/apply through MCP with deterministic state, no-op diffs, invalid/old versions, secret exclusions, target changes and partial failure.
Test persistence boundary and size/path limits using the existing filesystem/configuration seams where applicable.
Prove rejected or unsupported preset content cannot become a silently successful partial application.
items.out: Arbitrary OBS configuration backup, unrestricted files, full scene graph cloning, or storing stream credentials.

items.title: Evaluate OBS onboarding and distribution improvements against measured friction
items.problem: Published npm entry works, but startup diagnostics, client setup and platform-specific installation paths may still impose avoidable friction.
items.solution: Produce an evidence-backed distribution/onboarding decision and implementation-ready follow-up contracts for any selected improvement.
stories: I can distinguish OBS startup, credentials and MCP setup problems
I can enable the intended tools
explicit support for OBS startup and capture prerequisites
a platform claim is backed by execution
MCPB, native, container and editor packaging compared against user friction
backup and credential behavior stated before setup actions
onboarding does not silently alter my environment
a recorded adopt/defer/reject decision for each packaging direction
decisions: Audit existing npm, registry metadata, Docker/container support and client examples before proposing additions; preserve what is already working.
Evaluate MCPB first as a bounded desktop packaging candidate, and compare native binaries/Homebrew, Docker, VS Code/editor packaging and platform auto-start only for defined user jobs.
Separate connection diagnostics from starting OBS, changing obs-websocket settings, backup/restore or plugin installation.
Deliver a decision matrix with evidence, supported environments, costs, explicit dispositions and linked follow-up specs for any selected implementation.
Do not execute system/plugin installs or publish artifacts merely because this investigation is ready for an agent.
tests: Reproduce selected installation friction from an isolated clean consumer and compare the proposed path using exact attributable artifacts.
Verify existing lazy discovery versus ordinary OBS-connected startup in relevant client examples.
Acceptance for this issue is a bounded decision plus evidence; any selected code change must have a follow-up behavioral acceptance contract.
items.out: Automatic system configuration changes, a commitment to every packaging format, native-platform expansion without demand, or copying competitors' installers.

items.title: Audit transferable deadline, postcondition and OBS identity guarantees
items.problem: DCC exposes stronger explicit identity/deadline semantics, but the current server already has substantial cancellation and non-retry behavior, so the actual transferable gaps need precise evidence.
items.solution: Record an evidence-backed lifecycle contract that preserves existing guarantees and identifies only demonstrated or workflow-required additions.
stories: a lost response is not reported as successful completion
no unsafe replay of an in-flight mutation
a reconnect cannot duplicate side effects
deadlines remain meaningful across composed operations
postcondition evidence where a workflow promises confirmation
accepted requests are not confused with verified outcomes
working guarantees are not unnecessarily reimplemented
identity claims limited to what ordinary OBS WebSocket exposes
the server does not invent process identity
a clear decision on native instance binding
DCC's native-only contract is not mistaken for a simple configuration option
decisions: Inspect existing request correlation, cancellation, reconnect, event continuity, in-flight request and batch non-retry guarantees.
Compare pre-send failure, post-send uncertain outcome, readback/reconciliation, composed deadlines and intervening changes at the public contract.
Separate ordinary WebSocket connection/session evidence from exact OBS PID/plugin-instance/event-sequence guarantees that require a native extension.
Produce a gap/guarantee matrix, preserve-existing dispositions and bounded follow-up acceptance cases for needed improvements; no blanket client rewrite.
Provide the verified lifecycle assumptions required by the guided preview/apply work.
tests: Reuse actual protocol and packaged-process seams; extend only uncovered applied-but-reply-lost, deadline propagation or identity-change cases.
Inspect actual OBS state and returned errors, not generic bounded-response success predicates.
Do not assign observed passes to a missing native environment; label source reasoning and execution separately.
items.out: Implementing a native plugin, changing language/framework, adding automatic retries for uncertain mutations, or promising PID identity from standard requests.

items.title: Decide broader OBS product directions without losing deferred opportunities
items.problem: The study identifies valuable broader workflows whose dependencies and product costs exceed the next server milestone; without explicit dispositions they can disappear or become accidental scope.
items.solution: Maintain and resolve a bounded decision backlog for broader product directions, with evidence and follow-up contracts for selected work.
stories: every broader opportunity given an explicit disposition
window capture and private recording evaluated by platform
support claims reflect OBS and OS constraints
media/showrunner and visual verification workflows evaluated
the server can grow around useful jobs
readiness, confirmation and restoration considered together
coordination does not confuse local state with end-to-end signal
overlay, Stream Deck and transcription-assist options evaluated
a larger product is chosen deliberately
dashboard and AI-streamer directions considered with their dependencies
UI, chat, TTS and avatar work does not appear as hidden server scope
native OBS plugin and device-management costs recorded
architecture scores do not dictate an unnecessary platform change
each deferral has a revisit trigger and linked follow-up destination
decisions: Assess separately: recording/window capture helpers; status/showrunner/media sequencing and visual diff; multi-PC production; dashboards/TUI/embedded creator UI; overlays/Stream Deck/live transcription; AI streaming/chat/TTS/avatar; native OBS plugin and device/plugin/system management.
Use user jobs, platform/runtime evidence, maintenance burden and boundaries as decision criteria; scores and tool counts alone do not justify adoption.
Distinguish source-supported designs from verified runtime behavior, especially DCC native and BEA hosted workflows.
For every direction record adopt/defer/reject, rationale, prerequisites, revisit trigger, and a linked implementation spec if adopted.
Keep named event-confirmed workflow extensions separate from an unbounded generic scripting/event engine.
tests: Decision acceptance requires a traceable source finding and explicit disposition for every listed direction.
Use bounded prototypes or environment checks only when needed to resolve a specific decision; specify their observable success criteria first.
Do not claim production, platform or real-OBS verification from a source-only comparison.
items.out: Building all listed products, operating hosted accounts, installing plugins/services, or approving a rewrite solely from competitor rankings.

items.title: Adopt OBS competitor findings with complete traceability and release acceptance
items.problem: The research establishes concrete fidelity gaps and useful future directions, but a first milestone alone would leave later findings without accountable destinations.
items.solution: Deliver a dependable fidelity-and-visual milestone, track later guided workflows, and preserve every remaining finding through explicit investigations, existing-capability records or reasoned rejection.

decisions: Retain the existing TypeScript/Effect architecture and documented toolset/capability policy. Adopt independent design strengths through observable product contracts.
Use one parent tracker with five first-milestone implementation children, five later workflow/discovery children, and three bounded decision/audit children.
Keep the full finding-to-disposition map in this parent and a repository mirror. Every actionable finding has a linked destination, preserve-existing evidence, or explicit rejection rationale.
Historical comparative evidence remains pinned; new baseline and release evidence name their actual source and artifact.
Ready-for-agent indicates the spec is triaged, not that dependency-blocked or later-milestone work may start early.
Existing issue #2 is a reconciliation target, not a duplicate implementation task: verify its stated subscription and retention acceptance before closing or narrowing it.

Parent completion requires linked implementation children to meet acceptance and decision children to resolve every direction with explicit follow-ups or rejection. Unresolved later work keeps the parent open.
tests: Primary acceptance seam approved by the user: freshly installed package through MCP against controlled OBS, with focused existing protocol/HTTP tests where necessary and separate isolated real OBS/client visual verification before release.
Test external results, resulting OBS state, errors, bounds and artifact identity; avoid coupling assertions to module layout or tool counts.
Use the study's counterexamples as regression inputs after correcting known fixture-oracle limitations.
Audit finding coverage, dependencies, acceptance evidence and actual release attribution before marking milestones or parent complete.
items.out: Implementing production code during spec publication; promising all investigated product directions; native/framework rewrites; arbitrary execution; unbounded data collection; publishing npm packages without release authorization.
